questions.q: Statements: B ≤ F = J > N ≥ S < V ≤ Z > C = G Conclusions: I. N > Z II. Z ≥ F In this question, the relationship between different element is shown in the statements. The statements are followed by two conclusions. Give answer
options: If only conclusion I is true
If either conclusion I or II is true
If neither conclusion I nor II is true
If both conclusions I and II are true
questions.solution: From B <= F = J > N >= S < V <= Z > C = G, the chain between N and Z reverses direction at S < V, so no definite relation between N and Z can be established; conclusion I is false. Similarly F and Z are connected only through that reversed link, so Z >= F also cannot be confirmed. Neither conclusion follows. **Answer: If neither conclusion I nor II is true**
questions.shortcut: Chain signs reverse at S < V, so nothing crosses that point.

questions.q: Carefully read the given statements, followed by two conclusions labeled I and II. Treat the statements as true, even if they differ from commonly known facts, and determine which of the conclusions logically follow. Statements: K ≤ Z < X ≥ D; C ≥ D = M Conclusions: I. Z < C II. X ≥ M
options: If only conclusion I is true
If only conclusion II is true
If either conclusion I or II is true
If both conclusion I and II are true
questions.solution: From X >= D = M we directly get X >= M, so conclusion II follows. For Z < C, the available chains are K <= Z < X >= D and C >= D; the direction reverses at X >= D, so Z and C cannot be compared. Only conclusion II is true. **Answer: If only conclusion II is true**
questions.shortcut: X >= D = M settles II in one step.

questions.q: Statements: 2 < 4 ≤ 5 = 6 > 7 ,4 ≤ 1 > 9 < 8 < 3 Conclusions: I. 3 > 2 II. 2 > 7 In this question the relationship between different elements is shown in the statements. The statements are followed by conclusions. study the conclusions based on the given statements and select the appropriate answer
options: If only conclusion I is true.
If only conclusion II is true.
If either conclusion I or II is true.
If neither conclusion I nor II is true.
questions.solution: Combining the statements gives 3 > 8 > 9 < 1 >= 4 > 2 and 2 < 4 <= 5 = 6 > 7. For conclusion I, the chain from 3 to 2 reverses at 9 < 1, so 3 > 2 is not definite. For conclusion II, the chain from 2 to 7 reverses at 6 > 7, so 2 > 7 is also not definite. Neither conclusion follows. **Answer: If neither conclusion I nor II is true.**
questions.shortcut: Locate where each chain reverses; both conclusions sit past a reversal.

questions.q: How many boxes are kept above the box which contains comb?
questions.solution: Placing the clues together, the stack from top to bottom is: F-Perfume, B-Brush, D-Lipstick, E-Comb, C-Glass, A-Mirror. The comb is in box E, which is fourth from the top, so exactly three boxes are kept above it. **Answer: Three**
questions.shortcut: Fix D and C first, then hang the items off them.
questions.passage: Directions: Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Six boxes - A, B, C, D, E and F, each containing a different item, are stacked one above the other but not necessarily in the same order. The items are Mirror, Glass, Brush, Lipstick, Comb and Perfume. The box which contains mirror is kept three boxes below the box D. Only one box is kept between box C and box D. The box which contains brush is kept three boxes above box C. The number of boxes kept below the box which contains brush is two more than the number of boxes kept above the box which contains lipstick. Two boxes are kept between box A and the box which contains lipstick. The box which contains glass is kept immediately below the box which contains comb. Box F is kept above box B which doesn't contain Perfume and Comb. Box E is not kept below box C.

questions.q: Which of the following boxes contains Perfume?
questions.solution: The final arrangement from top to bottom is F-Perfume, B-Brush, D-Lipstick, E-Comb, C-Glass, A-Mirror. Box F is at the top and contains the perfume. **Answer: Box F**

questions.q: If Box C and Box A interchange their items, then which item is kept two boxes above the box which contains mirror?
questions.solution: In the final stack F-Perfume, B-Brush, D-Lipstick, E-Comb, C-Glass, A-Mirror, box C holds Glass and box A holds Mirror. After they interchange, the mirror sits in box C at position five, and two boxes above it is position three, where box D holds the Lipstick. **Answer: Lipstick**

questions.q: Four of the following five are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Find the one which doesn’t belong to the group?
questions.solution: In the final stack, for A-Glass, B-Perfume, D-Brush and C-Comb the named item is kept exactly one box above the named box. For E-Mirror, however, the mirror is in box A, two boxes below E, so this pair breaks the pattern. **Answer: E, Mirror**

questions.q: Which item is contained in Box D?
questions.solution: The unique stack is F-Perfume, B-Brush, D-Lipstick, E-Comb, C-Glass, A-Mirror from top to bottom, so box D contains the Lipstick. **Answer: Lipstick**

questions.q: What is the shortest distance between Point W and Point Y?
questions.solution: Tracking the walk on a grid: X(0,0) -> Y(18,0) -> Z(18,10) -> W(12,10). From W to Y the east-west gap is 6 m and the north-south gap is 10 m, so the shortest distance = sqrt(6^2 + 10^2) = sqrt(136) m, about 11.66 m. **Answer: √136 m**
questions.shortcut: Y and W share the same east-west level difference of 6 m and a 10 m north gap.
questions.passage: Directions: Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Priya started walking from Point X and walked 18 m to the east and reached Point Y. From Point Y, she turned left and walked 10 m to reach Point Z. From Point Z, she turned left again and walked 6 m to reach Point W. From Point W, Priya turned right and walked 12 m to reach Point V. From Point V, she turned right again and walked 8 m to reach Point R. From Point R, she turned left and walked 14 m to reach Point K.

questions.q: In which direction is Point W with respect to Point K?
questions.solution: The points are Y(18,0), Z(18,10), W(12,10), V(12,22), R(20,22) and K(20,36). W lies 8 m to the west and 26 m to the south of K, so W is to the south-west of K. **Answer: South-west**

questions.q: What is the total distance between Point K and Point Z?
questions.solution: Walking from K back to Z retraces the last four legs: K to R 14 m, R to V 8 m, V to W 12 m and W to Z 6 m. Total distance = 14 + 8 + 12 + 6 = 40 m. **Answer: 40m**

questions.q: How many pairs of letters are there in the word ‘ PHENOMENON’, each of which have as many letters between them (both forward and backward direction) as they have between them according to English alphabetical order?
questions.solution: For each pair of letters in PHENOMENON, compare the count of letters between them in the word with their distance in the alphabet. Checking all pairs, exactly five qualify - for example H (2nd) and N (8th) have five letters between them in the word and the alphabet gap H to N is also six places spanning the same span - giving five such pairs in total. **Answer: Five**
questions.shortcut: Only compare pairs whose word gap and alphabet gap are equal; skip pairs that fail at the first letter.

questions.q: Who among the following likes Pedagogy?
questions.solution: The chronological order works out to: A (9th June, Geology), D (22nd June, Psychology), E (9th July, History), C (22nd July, Economics), F (9th August, Sociology), B (22nd August, Pedagogy). Hence B likes Pedagogy. **Answer: B**
questions.passage: Directions: Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Six persons - A, B, C, D, E and F - were born on either the 9th or 22nd of three different months - June, July and August of the same year. Each person likes a different subject - Geology, Pedagogy, History, Psychology, Economics and Sociology. E was born two persons after the one who likes Geology. E was born on an odd date in a month having an odd number of days. The one who likes Sociology was born after E. A was born four persons before the one who likes Sociology. No person was born between A and D. D doesn't like Geology and History. More than two persons were born between D and the one who likes Pedagogy. F was born immediately after the person who likes Economics. F was not born on an even date. The one who likes History was born before F who was born before B.

questions.q: Which among the following statement(s) is/are not true? I. C was born on 9th July. II. The number of persons born before E was one less than the number of persons born after F. III. A likes Geology
questions.solution: In the final arrangement A-9th June-Geology, D-22nd June-Psychology, E-9th July-History, C-22nd July-Economics, F-9th August-Sociology, B-22nd August-Pedagogy. Statement I is false because C was born on 22nd July, not 9th July. Statement II is false because two persons were born before E while only one was born after F, and 2 is not one less than 1. Statement III is true since A likes Geology. So I and II are not true. **Answer: Both I and II**

questions.q: Who among the following was born on 22nd June?
questions.solution: In the final arrangement, 22nd June is D, and D likes Psychology. So the one who likes Psychology was born on 22nd June. **Answer: The one who likes Psychology.**

questions.q: Four of the following five are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Find the one which doesn’t belong to the group?
options: The one who was born two persons after C
questions.solution: The persons in the other four options - the one who likes History (E, 9th July), F (9th August), the one born two persons after C (B, 22nd August) and the one who likes Economics (C, 22nd July) - were all born in July or August. A alone was born in June, so A is the odd one. **Answer: A**

questions.q: How many persons were born between F and the person who likes Geology?
questions.solution: F was born 9th August (position five) and the Geology-liking person A was born 9th June (position one). Persons between them: D, E and C - three persons. **Answer: Three**

questions.q: Which container contains the lowest quantity of juice?
questions.solution: Since only E has less juice than C, E is the lowest and C (8 L) the second lowest. Only B and at most one more can be above 17 L, and the single container between B and A forces the order E < C(8) < A < F < B(17) < D. Hence E contains the lowest quantity of juice. **Answer: E**
questions.shortcut: C is fixed at 8 L with only E below it; the rest cascade from F > A and D >= F.
questions.passage: Directions: Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Six containers - A, B, C, D, E and F - contain different quantities of juice, but not necessarily in the same order. The quantity of juice in each container is an integer. E contains less juice than D but not more juice than C. Only one container contains less juice than C, and C contains 8 litres of juice. Not more than two containers contain more juice than B. F contains more juice than A. Only one container contains a quantity of juice between the quantities of juice contained in containers B and A. The quantity of juice A contains is an odd number. D doesn't contain less juice than F. B contains 17 litres of juice.

questions.q: If D contains 2 litres more juice than B and E contains 3 litres less juice than C, then what is the sum of the quantities of juice contained in D and E?
questions.solution: D = 17 + 2 = 19 L and E = 8 - 3 = 5 L. Sum = 19 + 5 = 24 litres. **Answer: 24 litres**

questions.q: If F contains 4 litres more juice than C, then what could be the possible quantity of juice in container A?
questions.solution: With F = C + 4 = 12 L, the order E < C(8) < A < F(12) < B(17) < D must hold, so A lies strictly between 8 and 12. A is odd, so A could be 9 or 11 litres. **Answer: Either 9 or 11 litres**

questions.q: Find the odd one out from the following options?
questions.solution: In DFHJ, JLNP, RTVX and HJLN each letter is two places ahead of the previous one. In KMPR the jump from M to P is three places, so KMPR is the odd one out. **Answer: KMPR**
questions.shortcut: Check letter skips: four options jump +2 every time.

questions.q: Which of the following statement is correct? I. Two married couples in the family II. H is child of U III. Males and females are equal in family
questions.solution: The family tree is: R and S are the parents of P and T; P (husband of Q) has two children X and H; T is married to U. Couples are R-S, P-Q and T-U, so there are three couples, not two - I is wrong. H is the child of P and Q, not of U - II is wrong. Males (R, P, U, X) and females (S, T, Q, H) are four each - III is correct. So only III is correct. **Answer: Only III**
questions.shortcut: Build the tree: R-S -> P, T; P+Q -> X, H; T+U.
questions.passage: Directions: Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. T is sister of P who has two children. X is grandson of R. Q is daughter-in-law of S who is spouse of R. Q's only sister-in-law is married to U who has no sibling. H is daughter of P whose mother is S.

questions.q: Who among the following is father-in-law of U?
questions.solution: Q's only sister-in-law is T (P's sister), and T is married to U. T's father is R, so R is U's father-in-law. **Answer: R**

questions.q: What is the relation of P with respect to X’s mother?
questions.solution: X's mother is Q (P's wife), so P is the husband of X's mother. **Answer: Husband**

questions.q: Four of the following five are alike in a certain way and form a group. Which of the following does not belong to the group?
questions.solution: The unique arrangement is row 1 (left to right): F, E, D, A, B, C, G and row 2: W, Y, U, X, V, S, T. E, D, X and V sit at the 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th seats of their rows - consecutive places - while G sits at the last seat, so G does not belong to the group. **Answer: G**
questions.passage: Directions: Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Fourteen persons sit in two parallel rows facing each other. A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in row 1 and face south, while S, T, U, V, W, X and Y sit in row 2 and face north. Each person in row 1 faces exactly one person from row 2 and vice versa. Y sits fourth to the left of S. The one who sits opposite to S sits immediate right of G. Three persons sit between G and D. F sits two places away from D. The one who sits opposite to F sits second to the left of U. V sits to the right of U. Three persons sit between V and W. Immediate neighbour of U faces A who sits second to the left of E. E doesn't face W. D is not an immediate neighbour of B. V is neither immediate neighbour of T nor faces C.

questions.q: What is the position of the one who faces T with respect to E?
questions.solution: T sits at the 7th seat of row 2 and is faced by G, the 7th person of row 1. E sits 2nd in row 1 and faces south, so G, being five seats away towards E's left-hand side, is fifth to the left of E. **Answer: Fifth to the left**

questions.q: Who among the following faces C?
questions.solution: In the final arrangement, C sits 6th in row 1 and is faced by S, who sits 6th in row 2. **Answer: S**

questions.q: How many persons sit between V and the one who faces F?
questions.solution: F sits 1st in row 1, so the one facing F is W, 1st in row 2. V sits 5th in row 2, and the persons between W (1st) and V (5th) are Y, U and X - three persons. **Answer: Three**

questions.q: If Y and T interchanged their positions and in the same way W and X interchanged their positions then who sits third to the left of Y?
questions.solution: After Y and T interchange, Y sits at the 7th seat of row 2; after W and X interchange, W sits at the 4th seat. Counting towards the left (lower seat numbers), the third seat from Y's new position is the 4th seat, occupied by W. **Answer: W**

questions.q: Who among the following persons is from Hyderabad?
questions.solution: C and F are together, and I and E are together; the constraints push C, F, E and I into Hyderabad (the only city allowed four persons). A is from Meghalaya, H joins neither Leh nor C's city, and D differs from F and G, giving Meghalaya = A, D, H and Leh = B, G. So both F and E are from Hyderabad. **Answer: Both F and E**
questions.shortcut: C-F and I-E must sit in the max-size city; A anchors Meghalaya.
questions.passage: Directions: Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Nine persons - A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H and I - are from three different cities: Leh, Meghalaya and Hyderabad. At least two and not more than four persons are from the same city. G and C are not from the same city. D and F are not from Leh. C and F are from the same city. D is neither from the same city as F nor from the same city as G. I and E are from the same city. E is not from the same city as D. A is from Meghalaya. Only one person is from the same city as B. H is neither from Leh nor from the same city as C.

questions.q: Which of the following group of persons is from Leh?
questions.solution: In the final grouping, Leh has exactly the two persons B and G, since only one person is from the same city as B. So the group from Leh is B and G. **Answer: B and G**

questions.q: Who among the following persons is from the same city as H?
questions.solution: H is from Meghalaya along with A and D, so D is from the same city as H. **Answer: D**

questions.q: Which among the following combination is/are correct?
questions.solution: The final grouping is Leh: B, G; Meghalaya: A, D, H; Hyderabad: C, E, F, I. Only the combination D - Meghalaya is correct. **Answer: D - Meghalaya**

questions.q: The number of persons from Hyderabad is _______ than the number of persons from Meghalaya?
questions.solution: Four persons (C, E, F, I) are from Hyderabad and three (A, D, H) from Meghalaya, so Hyderabad has one more person than Meghalaya. **Answer: One more**
